purityConverter.modeConvertDesc: Convert gold weight between different karats
purityConverter.modeAnalyzeDesc: Find pure gold & alloy content in your gold
purityConverter.modeMakeDesc: Calculate alloy needed to create lower karat gold
purityConverter.valueDisclaimer: Based on fine gold × today's {city} 24K rate per gram. Excludes making charges, GST, and wastage — use the <calc>gold calculator</calc> and <wastage>wastage tool</wastage> for a full jewellery bill.
purityConverter.makeNote: Note: This calculation shows the theoretical alloy needed. Actual jewellery making involves specific alloy compositions (copper, silver, zinc) based on desired color and properties.
purityConverter.makeWarning: Select a lower karat than {purity} to calculate alloy addition. You cannot make higher purity gold by adding alloy.
purityConverter.howWeCalculateIntro: We keep fine (pure) gold mass constant when converting between karats.
purityConverter.howWeCalculateBullet2: Equivalent weight at another karat = fine gold ÷ target karat %.
purityConverter.howWeCalculateBullet3: Approximate ₹ value uses fine gold × your city's 24K price per gram (metal only).
purityConverter.understandingIntro: Gold purity is measured in karats (K) or percentage. 24K is 99.9% pure gold. 22K gold contains 91.6% pure gold mixed with other metals for strength. This converter helps you understand equivalent weights when converting between purities.
purityConverter.bullet22k: 22K Gold — 91.6% pure, standard for Indian jewellery
purityConverter.bullet18k: 18K Gold — 75% pure, common in international markets
purityConverter.bullet14k: 14K Gold — 58.3% pure, popular in Western countries
purityConverter.understandingFooter: <calc>Calculate jewellery cost</calc> with different purities • <hallmark>Verify purity marks</hallmark>
purityConverter.faq1Question: How do I convert 22K gold to 24K gold?
purityConverter.faq1Answer: To convert 22K gold to 24K, multiply your 22K weight by 0.916 (the purity of 22K). For example, 10g of 22K gold contains 9.16g of pure 24K gold. Use our converter above with 'Convert Weight' mode for instant calculations.
purityConverter.faq2Question: What is the formula for gold purity conversion?
purityConverter.faq2Answer: The formula is: Equivalent Weight = (Original Weight × Original Purity %) ÷ Target Purity %. For example, converting 10g of 22K to 18K: (10 × 91.6%) ÷ 75% = 12.21g of 18K gold.
purityConverter.faq3Question: Why does weight increase when converting to lower karat?
purityConverter.faq3Answer: Lower karat gold contains less pure gold and more alloy metals. So the same amount of pure gold spreads across more total weight. Converting 10g of 24K to 22K gives you 10.91g because 22K has only 91.6% gold content.
purityConverter.faq4Question: How much alloy is in 22K gold?
purityConverter.faq4Answer: 22K gold contains 91.6% pure gold and 8.4% alloy metals (usually copper, silver, or zinc). This alloy makes the gold harder and more suitable for jewellery. Use our 'Analyze Purity' mode to see exact alloy content.
purityConverter.faq5Question: What is a Tola and how is it used in gold measurement?
purityConverter.faq5Answer: A Tola is a traditional South Asian unit of weight equal to 11.6638 grams. It's commonly used in India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh for measuring gold. Our calculator supports Tola along with grams, milligrams, and troy ounces.
purityConverter.faq6Question: Which gold purity is best for investment?
purityConverter.faq6Answer: 24K gold (99.9% pure) is best for investment as it holds maximum gold content and is easier to sell at market rates. 22K is preferred for jewellery due to better durability, while 18K offers a balance of purity and strength.

goldMarketPulse.compositeExplain: Weighted blend of RSI (25%), Moving Averages (20%), MACD (20%), Bollinger Bands (15%), Momentum (10%), and Volatility (10%).
goldMarketPulse.rsiExplain: Relative Strength Index measures speed and magnitude of recent price changes. Above 70 = overbought, below 30 = oversold.
goldMarketPulse.movingAveragesDesc: Price position relative to key simple moving averages (SMA).
goldMarketPulse.edu_rsiBody: RSI measures the speed and magnitude of recent price changes on a 0-100 scale. A value above 70 suggests the asset may be overbought (prices rose fast), while below 30 suggests oversold (prices dropped fast). It does not predict direction — it flags how stretched recent moves are.
goldMarketPulse.edu_macdBody: MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence) tracks the relationship between two exponential moving averages (12-day and 26-day). When the MACD line crosses above the signal line, momentum is shifting upward; when it crosses below, momentum is shifting downward. The histogram shows the gap between the two lines.
goldMarketPulse.edu_bollingerBody: Bollinger Bands consist of a 20-day moving average with upper and lower bands at 2 standard deviations. When price is near the upper band (%B close to 100%), it's at the high end of recent range. Near the lower band (%B close to 0%), it's at the low end. Bands widen during volatile periods and narrow during calm ones.
goldMarketPulse.edu_momentumBody: Rate of Change (ROC) measures the percentage price change over a specific period. A positive 30-day ROC means the price is higher than 30 days ago. It indicates the speed of price movement — a rising ROC means acceleration, a falling ROC means deceleration.
goldMarketPulse.edu_volatilityBody: Volatility measures how much the price fluctuates day-to-day, expressed as an annualized percentage. Low volatility (<8%) suggests stable prices. High volatility (>18%) suggests larger daily swings and more uncertainty. It does not indicate direction — just the magnitude of moves.
goldMarketPulse.edu_supportResistanceEduBody: Support is a price level where gold has recently found buyers (recent 60-day low). Resistance is where selling pressure appeared (recent 60-day high). These are not predictions — they are observations of where price has recently turned around.
goldMarketPulse.howWeCalculateTitle: How We Calculate the Composite Score
goldMarketPulse.howWeCalculateBody: The composite score (0-100) is a weighted average of six sub-scores, each derived from standard technical indicators applied to daily India 24K gold prices.
goldMarketPulse.howBullet1: RSI (25%): The 14-day RSI value maps directly to 0-100.
goldMarketPulse.howBullet2: Price vs Moving Averages (20%): How many of the four key SMAs the price sits above.
goldMarketPulse.howBullet3: MACD (20%): Whether the histogram is positive/negative and trending up/down.
goldMarketPulse.howBullet4: Bollinger %B (15%), Momentum (10%), and Volatility (10%) each contribute to the blend.
